notes: la culpa = the blame; tener la culpa = to be to blame.

sentences.text: El juez dijo que era culpable.
sentences.translation: The judge said he was guilty.

sentences.text: Las paredes de mi cuarto son azules.
sentences.translation: The walls in my room are blue.

sentences.text: El cielo está muy azul hoy.
sentences.translation: The sky is very blue today.

notes: el/la comandante.

sentences.translation: The commander wants to see you.

sentences.text: Es la comandante de la nave.
sentences.translation: She's the commander of the ship.

sentences.text: Me gustan las películas de acción.
Es hora de pasar a la acción.
Las acciones dicen más que las palabras.

notes: obra de arte = work of art; obra de teatro = play; obras = roadworks, construction.

sentences.text: Vamos a ver una obra de teatro.
sentences.translation: We're going to see a play.

notes: Not a question you ask (that is pregunta). es cuestión de = it's a matter of.
¿Le molesta si…? = Do you mind if…?

sentences.translation: I need the report for tomorrow.

sentences.text: Los informes están en la mesa.
sentences.translation: The reports are on the table.

sentences.text: La casa está cerca del río.
sentences.translation: The house is near the river.

sentences.text: Es uno de los ríos más largos del país.
sentences.translation: It's one of the longest rivers in the country.

notes: Agrees with the person: ¡Bienvenida! to a woman. dar la bienvenida = to welcome.

gloss: to touch; to play (music); to be someone's turn
notes: me toca = it's my turn. toqué: c becomes qu before e.

sentences.text: Toqué el agua y estaba fría.
sentences.translation: I touched the water and it was cold.

notes: o becomes ue: cuento. contar con = to count on.

sentences.text: No se lo cuentes a nadie.

notes: Also an adjective: ropa interior = underwear.

sentences.text: El interior de la casa es muy bonito.
sentences.translation: The inside of the house is very nice.
Check the inside of the car.

sentences.text: Viven en el interior del país.

notes: In Spain piso is more common.

sentences.translation: I live in a small apartment.

sentences.text: Mi apartamento está en el tercer piso.
sentences.translation: My apartment is on the third floor.

notes: Followed by the subjunctive: ojalá venga = I hope he comes.

sentences.translation: I wish I could help you.

notes: Perdona / Perdone = excuse me, sorry (informal / formal).

sentences.translation: I'm never going to forgive you.

notes: de golpe = suddenly, all at once.

sentences.translation: It was a very hard blow.

sentences.text: Recibió un golpe en la cabeza.
sentences.translation: He took a blow to the head.

sentences.text: Oí unos golpes en la puerta.
sentences.translation: I heard some knocks at the door.
There are many styles of music.
I work from nine to five.

notes: The core sense is for good / once and for all (se fue definitivamente); the definitely sense is common in Latin America and in dubbed films but sounds like an anglicism to many speakers in Spain.

sentences.text: Se fue a vivir a México definitivamente.
sentences.translation: He moved to Mexico for good.

sentences.text: Hay una bomba en el edificio.
sentences.translation: There's a bomb in the building.

notes: el/la guardia = the guard (person); estar de guardia = to be on duty.

sentences.text: Los guardias están en la puerta.
sentences.translation: The guards are at the door.
You have to be on guard.

sentences.text: Las pistolas están en la caja.
sentences.translation: The guns are in the box.

gloss: to try; to taste; to prove
notes: o becomes ue: pruebo. Try food or clothes; also to prove.
Su Majestad = Your / His / Her Majesty.

sentences.translation: His Majesty is waiting for you.

notes: en marcha = running, under way; ¡En marcha! = Let's go!

sentences.text: Mañana hay una marcha por la paz.
El plan ya está en marcha.
sentences.translation: The plan is already under way.

notes: en común = in common.
Further away than ese; also for the distant past: aquellos días = those days.

sentences.translation: Do you see that building over there?

sentences.text: Mi vuelo sale a las seis.
No tuve el valor de decírselo.
sentences.translation: I didn't have the courage to tell him.

sentences.text: Esa foto tiene mucho valor para mí.
sentences.translation: That photo means a lot to me.

notes: Agrees with the thing owned: la casa es suya.

sentences.text: El objetivo está en el edificio.
sentences.translation: The target is in the building.

notes: Only in de repente = suddenly.

sentences.text: De repente, se fue la luz.

notes: ¿Estás bromeando? = Are you kidding?

sentences.text: Mi padre siempre bromea con todo.
sentences.translation: My dad is always joking about everything.
I'll wait for you at the entrance.

sentences.text: Compré dos entradas para el partido.
sentences.translation: I bought two tickets for the game.

sentences.text: La entrada está detrás del edificio.
sentences.translation: The entrance is behind the building.

notes: el doble = twice as much.

sentences.text: Hay muchas máquinas en la fábrica.
sentences.translation: There are lots of machines in the factory.

sentences.text: Tiene una marca en el cuello.
sentences.translation: He has a mark on his neck.
She wears a chain around her neck.

notes: In questions it shows surprise or reproach: ¿Acaso…? = Is it that…? por si acaso = just in case.

sentences.translation: So it's my fault, is it?

notes: Always feminine, even for a man.

sentences.text: Hay muchas parejas en la playa.
sentences.translation: There are lots of couples on the beach.
This summer we're going to the seaside.

sentences.text: Pasaba los veranos con mis abuelos.
sentences.translation: I used to spend summers with my grandparents.

notes: Similar to listo.

sentences.translation: There are flowers in the garden.

gloss: you (informal, in Argentina and parts of Latin America)
notes: Used instead of tú in some countries, with its own verb forms: vos sos = tú eres.

sentences.translation: I want to go with you.

sentences.text: Hay muchas islas en esta zona.
sentences.translation: There are lots of islands in this area.

notes: e becomes ie: cierro. cerrar con llave = to lock.

sentences.text: El sol es malo para la piel.
sentences.translation: The sun is bad for your skin.

sentences.text: En invierno tengo la piel muy seca.
sentences.translation: In winter my skin gets very dry.
He has a lot of enemies.

notes: ¡Exacto! = Exactly!

sentences.translation: I don't remember the exact words.
It's time for justice to be done.

notes: e becomes ie: despierto. despertarse = to wake up (yourself).

sentences.translation: I don't want to wake the baby.
Why are you waking me up so early?

notes: hace calor = it's hot; tengo calor = I'm hot.
Usually referirse a: ¿A qué te refieres? = What do you mean?

sentences.translation: He took her by the arm.

notes: Often escaparse.

sentences.translation: We have to get out of here.
We got lost in the woods.

sentences.text: No vayas al bosque de noche.
sentences.translation: Don't go into the forest at night.

sentences.text: Hay muchos bosques en el norte.
sentences.translation: There are lots of forests in the north.

notes: tener visita = to have visitors.

sentences.text: Vi un movimiento detrás de la ventana.
sentences.translation: I saw something move behind the window.

notes: ser rico = to be rich; estar rico = to taste good.
Almost always in a pesar de = despite. Also the verb pesar = to weigh.

sentences.text: A pesar de todo, te quiero.
Salimos a pesar de la lluvia.
sentences.translation: We went out despite the rain.

sentences.text: A pesar de eso, es buena persona.
sentences.translation: Even so, he's a good person.

notes: en absoluto = not at all.

sentences.translation: I have absolute confidence in you.
It doesn't bother me at all.

notes: Always plural: de vacaciones = on vacation.

sentences.translation: Where are you going on vacation?
Shall we go to the movies tonight?

sentences.text: Te espero en la puerta del cine.
sentences.translation: I'll wait for you outside the cinema.

notes: Used in Spain with vosotros; in Latin America use su.

sentences.text: Me gusta todo, especialmente el café.
sentences.translation: I like everything, especially the coffee.
I made it especially for you.

notes: False friend: embarrassed = avergonzado.

sentences.translation: How long have you been pregnant?

notes: Usually plural: los pantalones.
en defensa propia = in self-defense.

sentences.text: En mi defensa, no lo sabía.
sentences.translation: In my defense, I didn't know.

sentences.text: Las defensas de la ciudad son fuertes.
Tu madre es una mujer estupenda.
sentences.translation: Your mother is a wonderful woman.
I'm under a lot of pressure.

sentences.text: Hay mucha presión en el trabajo.
sentences.translation: There's a lot of pressure at work.

notes: el/la testigo.

sentences.translation: The soldiers arrived in the village.

notes: Resulta que… = It turns out that…

sentences.translation: It turns out you were right.
It turned out to be a good plan.
In the end everything turned out fine.

notes: depender de = to depend on.
Also an adjective: inglés, inglesa = English (person, thing).

sentences.text: Mi inglés no es muy bueno.

notes: los estudios = studies, education. estudio is also 'I study'.

sentences.text: Trabaja en un estudio de música.
sentences.translation: He works in a music studio.
I don't know how to express my feelings.

notes: a propósito = on purpose; also 'by the way'.

sentences.translation: By the way, how's your mother?

sentences.text: ¿Cuál es el propósito de todo esto?
sentences.translation: What's the purpose of all this?

gloss: to leave, set off; to split
notes: a partir de = from, starting (a partir de hoy = from today on). parte is also the noun 'part'.

sentences.text: A partir de mañana, todo cambia.

sentences.translation: He split the bread in two.
